newsitem.title: UK: Brazil c.bank official says rating rise overdue.
newsitem.headline: Brazil c.bank official says rating rise overdue.

text.p: An increase in Brazil's single-B ratings from Moody's and Standard & Poor's was overdue, a senior central bank official told bankers at a meeting here.
"Rating agencies having an overrated memory for the past in the way they see Brazil," said Gustovo Franco, director of international affairs at the Central Bank of Brazil.
"They tell us they are slow to move down and up, but I believe it is about time (we had an upgrade)," he said.
Franco was talking to investors about Brazil's economy and debt management in the final leg of a roadshow for a $750 million global bond, due for launch next Monday.
Brazil's long-term foreign currency debt is rated B1 by Moody's and B-plus, with a positive outlook by S&P. Other ratings include a B-plus from IBCA, and BB-minus from Duff & Phelps.
"Looking at Brazil right now, ignoring the past, the question is what is wrong with this country that it is not investment grade," Franco said.

"What else do we have to do to get an upgrade? We have been underrated for very long, and (our debt) has been trading well inside countries that have ratings sometimes three notches over Brazil, and that is nonsense," he said.
Speculation about an upgrade in Brazil's foreign-currency debt swept the Brady market earlier this month, leading to sharp price gains in its debt.
Througout the 1980s and into the 1990s, Brazil's economy suffered high inflation and recession.

The introduction of a radical reform programme called the Real Plan in 1994 stabilised the country, with inflation falling from over 9,000 percent in 1993 to a forecast of around 10 percent in 1996, Franco said.
He said Brazil's budget situation and inflation and GDP growth figures were similar to many other economies.
"The positition of the rating agencies is that a strong memory in an important thing," Franco said.
"It wears off with time, and we have to be patient. And I have no doubt we will be investment grade at some point in the future," he said.
Duff & Phelps assigned its BB-minus rating to Brazil's upcoming bond earlier this week.
It said the rating reflected the government's commitment to overall macroeconomic stability and structural reform under the real plan.
